narrative.overview: Lamie feels like a quiet florist's lookbook assembled from warm paper, botanical color fields, restrained typography and real flower imagery. Editorial scale creates personality on storytelling surfaces while catalog and detail views become calmer, denser galleries.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper canvases with ink-brown type.
Lora headlines paired with precise Be Vietnam Pro UI copy.
Broad editorial rhythm on Home; compact task rhythm in catalog.
Dusty rose and botanical sage used as supporting fields.
Selective transform-based motion with reduced-motion support.

rules.name: The Flower Leads Rule
rules.body: UI colors remain muted; saturated hues belong to approved product photography.

rules.name: The Ink Is Scarce Rule
rules.body: Full ink backgrounds mark major narrative or conversion moments, not every container.

rules.name: The Wide Headline Rule
rules.body: Prefer a broad two- or three-line editorial composition over a narrow stack of many short lines.

rules.name: The Honest Label Rule
rules.body: Labels describe state or source; they are not decorative eyebrow copy.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Try a paper shade or rule before adding a shadow.

rules.name: The Transform-Only Motion Rule
rules.body: Animate opacity and transforms; never animate layout dimensions.

dos: Do let approved flower photography be the strongest chromatic element.
Do keep desktop hero headings to two lines and mobile hero headings to three or fewer.
Do use paper rules and negative space to group information.
Do preserve visible focus, reduced motion and truthful demo/source labels.
Do keep task-heavy catalog views denser than narrative Home sections.
donts: Don't introduce gradients, glass cards, excessive pills or card-inside-card layouts.
Don't animate width, height, margin or padding.
Don't add testimonials, prices, delivery promises or policies without approved source data.
Don't use decorative section numbers where there is no real sequence.
Don't let a sticky control cover a heading, focus target or the end of the page.
